## Summary

Track Durable work and native clients as 32 independently reviewable child issues, preserving the original approved round boundary and its evidence requirements.

Parent: [ROADMAP](https://github.com/trungtaottn/cf-agent-hub/issues/2). Original plan: `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-10-23-r2-durable-work.md`. Canonical capability IDs: F11, F12, F13, F14, F15, F16, F17, F18, F19, F20, F21, F22, F23, F24, F25, F26, F29, F34, F40.

## Problem / motivation

The original round remains specified. These issues describe future implementation and evidence, with explicit producers for unresolved contracts. Proposed files are not claimed to exist in the current R1 candidate. The source task register is too coarse for safe pickup by multiple agents: individual issues need explicit ownership, transaction boundaries, prerequisites and observable acceptance criteria. Splitting a checklist does not authorize changing native contracts or moving a capability into an earlier round.

## Proposed flow

1. Read the round plan, the exact published baseline and the child’s typed dependencies before selecting work.
2. Complete contract/interface producers first, then assign one implementation owner per shared transaction or registry surface. Use isolated branches and serialize shared integration points.
3. Run the child’s specified verification when implementing it, retain actual observed results and independently review the bounded deliverable.
4. Join all required evidence at [R2-ACCEPT](https://github.com/trungtaottn/cf-agent-hub/issues/49); keep status pending when an environment, protocol client, owner decision or evidence is missing.
5. Update this index with real issue outcomes. Closing an implementation child does not automatically promote the entire round.

## Scope

**In scope**

All original 12 tasks mapped below, their reviewed subtask boundaries, current-source corrections, negative/race/recovery criteria and the complete acceptance handoff. Runtime implementation consumes the preceding independently accepted round. R4 branch-level contract drafting may proceed independently where the original plan explicitly permits it; acceptance and all runtime consumers retain their stated gates.

**Out of scope / non-goals**

Product implementation or test execution during backlog creation; silent contract redesign; duplicate authorization/replay/recovery engines; reclassifying old local evidence as a newer candidate’s result; automatic merge, deployment or release.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Every child below has its required source/code/evidence deliverable independently reviewed, or an explicit approved scope decision recorded.
- [ ] All original task and capability coverage remains intact; no deferred implementation is marked done solely because its issue exists.
- [ ] Dependency, current-authority, transaction, privacy and recovery boundaries survive integration across children.
- [ ] [R2-ACCEPT](https://github.com/trungtaottn/cf-agent-hub/issues/49) records the complete exact-candidate gate before round status advances to Verified.

## Touchpoints

- `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-10-23-r2-durable-work.md` and `validation/implementation-plan-register.json` are the approved planning source.
- `docs/feature-matrix.md`, `docs/roadmap.md`, `docs/testing.md` and `docs/release-checklist.md` define capability and evidence boundaries.
- Candidate inspected: `22226633284e6410b2724acfcbfe1fe32f9325cc`; its publication status and known gaps are recorded in [R1-PUBLISH](https://github.com/trungtaottn/cf-agent-hub/issues/7) and [R1-DOCS](https://github.com/trungtaottn/cf-agent-hub/issues/9).

A parent link is organizational, not a predecessor that creates a dependency cycle. Queue priority never overrides readiness. No assignee or due date is invented.

title: [R2] Durable work and native clients — execution epic

body:
## Summary

Prepare a reviewed additive R2 plan amendment that matches the real R1 storage, command, client, recovery and verification boundaries before implementation begins.

Parent: [R2](https://github.com/trungtaottn/cf-agent-hub/issues/4). Original plan coverage: R2-T01, R2-T12. Capability coverage: F14, F20, F24, F41.

## Problem / motivation

The old R2 plan proposes 0002-durable-work.sql, but the retained R1 candidate already installs migrations 0001 through 0007. Its shared bounded recovery requirements must be reconciled with the final implemented interfaces and later R1 receipt amendment, together with the current generated-contract/test discovery layout. scripts/verify-release.mjs:133 currently accepts only --round R1; R2-T12-D must implement additive R2 policy/schema/CLI support before the planned R2 command is runnable. Following it literally can collide with an installed migration or produce a false green command that never collects the new tests. This issue owns plan reconciliation; the R2 shared-boundary/storage children own code changes.

## Proposed flow

1. Compare the published R1 source and accepted handoff with every R2 proposed path, command and migration assumption; record existing versus planned surfaces explicitly.
2. Amend migration instructions to use one assigned next-unused version, 0008 only if the actual baseline remains unchanged, and name a single owner for storage registration.
3. Document extensions needed for canonical generated roots, auth/audit/cursor/recovery registries and actual test-runner discovery, linking the relevant R2 child issues. Explicitly link [R2-T12-D](https://github.com/trungtaottn/cf-agent-hub/issues/47) as the owner of additive --round R2 release-verifier support.
4. Record additive reviewed amendments and updated dependency/coverage references while preserving historical receipts and the R1-ACCEPT gate.
5. Recheck the amendment at the final R1 acceptance handoff; drift after drafting must be reconciled before a consumer starts.

## Scope

**In scope**

Source-grounded plan corrections and the interface handoff for all twelve original R2 tasks.

**Out of scope / non-goals**

Implementing R2 before Verified R1, creating a second transaction owner, overwriting existing migration files, or rewriting old approvals to approve new scope.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Every R2 path/command assumption is classified current, planned or superseded with concrete source evidence.
- [ ] Migration numbering cannot collide with the installed R1 schema and one child owns the shared migration/registry integration.
- [ ] Future check commands explicitly collect R2 agent/runtime/task/artifact/search/import/CLI suites; the plan does not mistake no tests found for success.
- [ ] A separate amendment review/digest is recorded, and all R2 runtime work remains gated by R1-ACCEPT.

## Touchpoints

- Existing candidate: `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-10-23-r2-durable-work.md`.
- Existing candidate: `src/storage/migrations.ts`.
- Existing candidate: `scripts/generate-auth-contract.mjs`.
- Existing candidate: `vitest.config.ts`.
- Existing candidate: `vitest.workers.config.ts`.
